section_summary: This section contains the concluding portions of a comprehensive American consular report prepared by Vice Consul John K. Emmerson on the 'Kōminka' (Japanization) movement in Taiwan, along with Department of State commendation instructions. It examines colonial governance, police supervision, schooling, language assimilation, and social reforms directed at both the indigenous aboriginal population and Formosan Chinese society, while evaluating the prospects and limitations of assimilation. The section also includes an aboriginal population distribution map, notes on local administration, a Japanese terminology glossary, a bibliography of sources, and two March 1940 instructions from Assistant Secretary Breckinridge Long awarding the report an 'Excellent' rating.

subfiles.about: Concluding section of a comprehensive consular report examining Japanese assimilation policy ('Kōminka') toward the indigenous aborigines and Chinese population of Taiwan.
subfiles.from: American Consulate, Taihoku, Taiwan (prepared by John K. Emmerson)
subfiles.summary: This concluding part of the consular report covers Japanese colonial policy toward Taiwan's indigenous tribes (Takasago), detailing police supervision, language instruction, resettlement, and suppression of indigenous customs and religious activities. It then evaluates the broader future of the Kōminka (Japanization) campaign among Formosan Chinese, noting language barriers, discrimination in secondary and higher education, and the monopolization of desirable administrative and professional jobs by Japanese. The document concludes with an overview of provincial and prefectural administration, an extensive glossary of Japanese colonial terms, and an annotated bibliography of official and academic sources.
subfiles.title: 'Kominka' or the Japanization of the People of Taiwan (Part VII, Part VIII, Notes, Glossary, and Bibliography)

subfiles.about: Instruction from the Department of State notifying Consul Gerald Warner that John K. Emmerson's report on Kōminka received an 'Excellent' rating.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State Breckinridge Long writes to American Consul Gerald Warner at Taihoku, commending the Consulate's report dated November 27, 1939, entitled ''Kominka' or the Japanization of the People of Taiwan' prepared by John K. Emmerson. The Department of State has accorded the report a rating of 'EXCELLENT'. Long notes that a copy of the instruction is also being sent to the American Consul General at Osaka, where Emmerson was subsequently transferred.
subfiles.title: Instruction to American Consul at Taihoku regarding Rating of John K. Emmerson's Report on Kōminka
subfiles.to: Gerald Warner, American Consul, Taihoku, Taiwan

subfiles.about: Instruction from the Department of State to the American Consul General at Osaka commending Vice Consul John K. Emmerson's report on Taiwan.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State Breckinridge Long notifies the American Consul General at Osaka that John K. Emmerson's report on 'Kominka' or the Japanization of the People of Taiwan has been rated 'EXCELLENT' by the Department of State. He praises the report as extraordinarily thorough and valuable to the Department, and instructs that the commendation be formally brought to Emmerson's attention.
subfiles.title: Instruction to American Consul General at Osaka Commending John K. Emmerson's Report on Kōminka
